title: The Future-Proof AI Playbook
kicker: A practical guide for business owners using AI tools and agents
subtitle: On 12 Nov 2026, Nvidia announced Jensen Huang's resignation as CEO, with CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO. Your AI tools don't stop when a leader changes, but it's a good moment to check how your AI is built.

overview.heading: The four rules at a glance
overview.intro: Each rule is a design choice you make once, so no single vendor, model or price change can stop your business.
rows: Which tools are critical, and who owns each one.

rules.label: What makes it reliable
rules.heading: Three habits that keep AI dependable

items.title: Write it down
items.text: Each workflow has a one-page description: trigger, steps, tools, owner.

items.title: Test the switch
items.text: Each quarter, run one workflow on a backup model, so switching is routine.

items.title: Log and review
items.text: Every AI action is logged, and you review the log weekly.

workflows.name: Rule 1 · Don't panic, check
workflows.goal: Know in ten minutes which of your AI tools matter most, and that they're still running.
workflows.trigger: Big news about an AI company, a price change, or an outage.
steps: List every AI tool you use: chatbot, WhatsApp replies, email assistant, CRM notes.
Mark each one: critical, useful or nice-to-have.
Check the vendor's official status page or newsroom, not social media.
Note any announced change to price, terms or availability, and decide if action is needed.
tools: Email or WhatsApp to the tool owner
workflows.approval: you decide what is critical. Nothing changes without your go-ahead.

workflows.name: Rule 2 · No lock-in to one model
workflows.goal: If one AI model gets pricier or slower, you swap it in minutes, not months.
workflows.trigger: A model's price, speed, quality or terms change.
steps: Build agents with a model setting, not a model baked into every step.
Keep two approved models for each workflow, a main one and a backup.
Store prompts outside the tool, so they work with either model.
Test the backup model on real examples before you switch.
tools: Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini or open models
n8n, Make or Zapier, or a custom agent
A small sheet of sample inputs and expected outputs
workflows.approval: you approve which models are allowed and when to switch.

workflows.name: Rule 3 · Own your workflow
workflows.goal: Your data, prompts and steps stay with you, not stuck inside one tool.
workflows.trigger: You start any new AI workflow, or renew a tool subscription.
steps: Keep customer data in your own CRM or database, not only inside the AI tool.
Save every prompt and template in a shared document you control.
Write the workflow steps down: trigger, actions, rules, owner.
Check that you can export your data and settings, and test the export once.
tools: Your CRM, Google Sheets or database
Scheduled exports to your own drive
workflows.approval: you control access and exports. Vendors never hold the only copy.

workflows.name: Rule 4 · Human in control
workflows.goal: The agent does the work, and you approve what matters.
workflows.trigger: The agent drafts anything that affects money, customers or your brand.
steps: Decide which actions are automatic (replies within approved templates) and which need you.
Route quotes, discounts, refunds and unusual requests to you for approval.
Approve, edit or reject in one tap from WhatsApp or email.
Log every action, so you can review what the agent did and why.
tools: Your CRM or a Google Sheet
A one-page policy the agent follows
workflows.approval: anything involving money, commitments or exceptions waits for you.
